{{nihongo|'''Hioka Shrine'''|日岡神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

}}'''Hioka Shrine'' (Hioka Shrine) is located in Ono, Kakogawa Town, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}{{ill|Kakogawa, Hyōgo|ar|كاكوغاوا (هيوغو)|az|Kakoqava|azb|کاکوقاوا، هیوقو|bg|Какогава|ce|Какогава|ceb|Kakogawachō-honmachi|cs|Kakogawa (Hjógo)|de|Kakogawa|eo|Kakogava|es|Kakogawa|et|Kakogawa|fa|کاکوگاوا، هیوگو|fi|Kakogawa|fr|Kakogawa|ga|Kakogawa|gl|Kakogawa|it|Kakogawa|ja|加古川市|ko|가코가와시|lt|Kakogava|mg|Kakogawachō-honmachi|mzn|هاکوگاوا، هیوگو|nl|Kakogawa|no|Kakogawa|pl|Kakogawa|pt|Kakogawa|ro|Kakogawa|ru|Какогава|sh|Kakogava|simple|Kakogawa, Hyōgo|sr|Какогава|sv|Kakogawa|tg|Какогава|th|คาโกงาวะ|tl|Kakogawa, Hyōgo|tr|Kakogawa|tt|Какогава|uk|Какоґава|ur|کاکوگاوا، ہیوگو|uz|Kakogawa|vi|Kakogawa, Hyōgo|war|Kakogawa, Hyōgo|zh|加古川市|zh_classical|加古川市|zh_min_nan|Kakogawa-chhī|zh_yue|加古川|qid=Q750569}}. In {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Overview ===
It is located at the southern foot of the hill on the left bank of {{ill|Kako River (Japan)|Q11398501|qid=Q11398501}} in southern Hyogo Prefecture. This hill has been called ``Hioka'' since ancient times, and it is also related to the origin of the area's place name ``Kago.''

The ``God of Hioka'' can be found in ``{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|Q11498726|qid=Q11498726}}'' of {{ill|Nara period|af|Nara-tydperk|ar|فترة نارا|bcl|Panahon nin Nara|bg|Нара (период)|bn|নারা যুগ|ca|Període Nara|ckb|سەردەمی نارا|cs|Období Nara|de|Nara-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Νάρα|eo|Epoko de Nara|es|Período Nara|eu|Nara aroa|fa|دوره نارا|fi|Nara-kausi|fr|Époque de Nara|gl|Período Nara|he|תקופת נארה|hr|Nara (razdoblje)|hu|Nara-kor|id|Zaman Nara|it|Periodo Nara|ja|奈良時代|jv|Periodhe Nara|ko|나라 시대|lt|Nara laikotarpis|ml|നാറ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Nara|nl|Naraperiode|nn|Naratida|no|Nara-perioden|oc|Periòde de Nara|pl|Nara (okres)|ps|نارا|pt|Período Nara|ro|Perioada Nara|ru|Период Нара|sh|Nara period|simple|Nara period|sk|Obdobie Nara|sl|Obdobje Nara|sr|Нара период|sv|Naraperioden|th|ยุคนาระ|tl|Panahong Nara|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Nala|tr|Nara Dönemi|uk|Період Нара|ur|نارا دور|vi|Thời kỳ Nara|war|Panahon Nara|wuu|奈良时代|zh|奈良時代|zh_min_nan|Nara sî-tāi|zh_yue|奈良時代|qid=Q189178}}, making it an old shrine that has been worshiped since ancient times. Currently, the enshrined deity Tenisasahiko-no-Mikoto is {{ill|Harima no Inabi no Ōiratsume|fa|هاریما نو اینابی نو اوایراتسومه|ja|播磨稲日大郎姫|zh|播磨稻日大郎姬|qid=Q11078587|lt=Harima Inahi-Taro-hime-no-Mikoto}} (the 12th {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ar|الإمبراطور كيكو|arz|الامبراطور كيكو|azb|کیکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Keikō|cs|Keikó|de|Keikō|es|Keikō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیکو|fr|Keikō (empereur)|hr|Keikō|hu|Keikó japán császár|id|Kaisar Keikō|it|Keikō|ja|景行天皇|ka|კეიკო|ko|게이코 천황|nds|Keikō|nl|Keiko (keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|simple|Emperor Keikō|sl|Cesar Kejko|sv|Keiko (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเคโก|tl|Emperador Keikō|tr|Keikō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейко|uz|Imperator Keikō|vi|Thiên hoàng Keikō|yo|Emperor Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723}}{{ill|Empress consort|Q7723211|qid=Q7723211}}) is widely worshiped in the Higashiharima area as the god of safe childbirth, based on a shrine tradition that says that he prayed for a safe childbirth.According to a legend from the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the construction project of {{ill|Kusatani RIver|Q24874726|qid=Q24874726|lt=Gogai Irrigation}}, the main irrigation water on the left bank of the Kako River, was carried out jointly by Hyuga Myojin (the deity of Hioka) and Prince Shotoku|Q263972}}. This was from the 1300s to the 1310s at the end of the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, and was founded by {{jalink|Shingon Risshu|Q580527}, who later became a confidant of {{ill|Emperor Go-Daigo|Q313942|qid=Q313942}}. }} (Shingon Ritsu sect has a deep-rooted belief in Prince Shotoku) There is a theory that the construction work carried out by {{ill|Monkan-bō Kōshin|Q11500110|qid=Q11500110|lt=Monkanbo Hiroma}}, a monk of {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|Q550182|qid=Q550182}}, has become legendary. It is also said that one of Bunkan's grandfathers was a priest at Hioka Shrine.

(Hyuga mythology)|Q3082751|Tamayorihime no Mikoto}}, Takanosabuki Fuai no Mikoto on the left, Isazahiko no Mikoto on the right (the origin tradition is { (See section {jalink|#Soken||Soken}}), after which it returned to Tenisasahiko no Mikoto, which appears in the above-mentioned ``Engishiki'' {{Sfn|Hioka Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. This "Ten Isahiko" is a god that does not appear in classical historical materials, and the ancient documents at Hioka Shrine were destroyed in a military fire in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}6 ({{ill|1578|Q6707|qid=Q6707}}), so its origin is not clear {{Sfn|Hioka Zaten Isahiko Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1980}}. One theory compares Amaisa Sahiko to Hiko Isasa Serihiko (real name of {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|Q65318|qid=Q65318}}), and writes "{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}" {{j alink|Emperor Korei|Q313041}} There is a theory that links it with the legend of the dispatch of Kibitsuhiko, which appears in the diary, but it is not certain as there are also theories that question this {{Sfn|Hioka Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.In addition, in recent shrine legends, {{ill|Harima no Inabi no Ōiratsume|fa|هاریما نو اینابی نو اوایراتسومه|ja|播磨稲日大郎姫|zh|播磨稻日大郎姬|qid=Q11078587|lt=Harima Inahitarohime no Mikoto}} (Harima no Inabi no Oiratsume no Mikoto: the 12th {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ar|الإمبراطور كيكو|arz|الامبراطور كيكو|azb|کیکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Keikō|cs|Keikó|de|Keikō|es|Keikō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیکو|fr|Keikō (empereur)|hr|Keikō|hu|Keikó japán császár|id|Kaisar Keikō|it|Keikō|ja|景行天皇|ka|კეიკო|ko|게이코 천황|nds|Keikō|nl|Keiko (keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|simple|Emperor Keikō|sl|Cesar Kejko|sv|Keiko (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเคโก|tl|Emperador Keikō|tr|Keikō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кейко|uz|Imperator Keikō|vi|Thiên hoàng Keikō|yo|Emperor Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723}} Empress) When {jalink|Ousu no Mikoto}} and Ousu no Mikoto ({{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258}}) and others gave birth to twins, the enshrined deity Tenisasahiko no Mikoto is said to have prayed for a safe delivery, and is now worshiped as the god of safe childbirth.<ref name="historical book"/>.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
Founding date is unknown. According to the shrine's legend, when {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188}} was on a conquest to the east, Arashenjin caused evil deeds and caused trouble, but due to a plan by Isazabe no Mikoto of {{ill|Kunitsukami|Q60995523|qid=Q60995523}}, he was able to get rid of Arashenjin. However, Isazabe-no-Mikoto was killed in battle, so the Emperor assigned Isazabe-no-Mikoto to the two pillars of prayer for victory in battle, Tamayorihime and Kusafuai-no-Mikoto (Emperor Jinmu's parents), and enshrined these three pillars. Suppose this is the case. On the other hand, although the basis for this is not clear, there is a theory that it was founded in {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}}2 ({{ill|730|Q23563|qid=Q23563}}). </ref>.

[[File:Hiokaryo Kofun haisho.JPG|thumb|240px|right|{{center|{{ill|Hioka Goryo Kofun|ja|日岡陵古墳|qid=Q11505277}} ({{ill|Harima no Inabi no Ōiratsume|fa|هاریما نو اینابی نو اوایراتسومه|ja|播磨稲日大郎姫|zh|播磨稻日大郎姬|qid=Q11078587|lt=Harima Inahitarohime Mikoto}}Ryo)}}]]The precincts are located at the southern foot of Mt. Hioka, and it is known that Mt. Hioka is home to a group of kofun from the early to middle {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}} period (Hioka kofun group/Hiokayama kofun group). Among them, the most representative one is {{ill|Hioka Goryo Kofun|ja|日岡陵古墳|qid=Q11505277}} ({{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|Q11268718|qid=Q11268718}}, mound length approximately 85.5 meters). There is a theory that it is associated with the ``hirehaka'' found in the Kako-gun section of ``Harima no Kuni Fudoki,'' and based on this theory, it is currently designated as the tomb of Harima Inahitarohime no Mikoto, the empress of Emperor Keiko.

=== Outline ===
In the literature, as mentioned above, in the Kako-gun-jo section of ``{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|Q11498726|qid=Q11498726}},'' which was established around the first year of {{ill|Reiki (era)|Q1373115|qid=Q1373115}} ({{ill|715|Q23528|qid=Q23528}}), there is a reference to the deity enshrined in Hioka {{Sfn|Hioka Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} 5 years ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}} link|Harima Province|Q1047523}}{{ill|Kako District, Hyōgo|Q1042066|qid=Q1042066|lt=Kago District}}, it is written as "Hioka Zaten Isahiko Shrine" and is listed in {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} {{Sfn|Hioka Shrine (Heibonsha)|1999}}.

In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}6 ({{ill|1578|Q6707|qid=Q6707}}), it is said that the shrine building and old records were destroyed by military fire, but the situation before then is not known. Also, in the first year of {{ill|Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161}} ({{ill|1764|Q7659|qid=Q7659}}), the shrine building was rebuilt by the people of Ono Village, Kawahara Village, and Mizoguchi Village.{{Sfn|Hioka Shrine (Heibonsha)|1999}}.After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in February of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}7 ({{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}}) {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Magazine Materials|1912}} ranked as {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} in {jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}. The shrine building was renovated and rebuilt in the 3rd year of Meiji ({{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}}), but in 1944 ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}) It was destroyed in a fire in 1969|Q2485}}, and the current shrine building was rebuilt in 1969 ({{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}}){{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Journal |1912}}. The name of the shrine was called ``Shoichii Hyuga Daimyojin'' in the early modern period, and was renamed ``Hioka Shrine'' after the Meiji period, but it is still commonly known locally as ``Hinata-san,'' ``Ohno-san,'' and ``Hioka-san.''

=== Gogai construction legend ===
According to the legend in the "Gogai origin story" written in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} (composed around October 3rd year ({{ill|1657|Q6987|qid=Q6987}})), the lower reaches of the {{ill|Kako River (Japan)|Q11398501|qid=Q11398501}} {{ill|Kusatani RIver|Q24874726|qid=Q24874726|lt=Gogai Irrigation}}, which is the backbone of the left bank of the area, is said to have been built by Hyuga Myojin (the deity of Hioka Shrine) and {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|Q263972|qid=Q263972}} in unison.{{sfn|Kaneko|2019|pp=13–15}}. Because the agreement was made at the ``Aragase Futsubashi Bridge'' near {{ill|Hioka Goryo Kofun|ja|日岡陵古墳|qid=Q11505277|lt=Hyugayama}}, it is said that this bridge came to be called by another name, ``Dango Bridge'' {{sfn|Kaneko|2019|pp=13–15}}.Japanese history researcher Tetsu Kaneko was a monk of the {{ill|Shingon Risshu|Q580527|qid=Q580527}} and {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|Q550182|qid=Q550182}} who was active from the end of the {{ill|13th century|Q7049|qid=Q7049}} to the middle of the {{ill|14th century|Q7034|qid=Q7034}}. {{ill|Emperor Go-Daigo|Q313942|qid=Q313942}}'s confidant {{ill|Monkan-bō Kōshin|Q11500110|qid=Q11500110|lt=Monkanbo Hiroma}} suggests that one of his grandfathers may have been a priest at Hioka Shrine.{{sfn|Kaneko|2019|p=22}}. Additionally, the Gogai Canal Repair Project, which is thought to have been carried out during this period, was carried out by Bunkan from the 1300s to the 1310s at Saidaiji Temple in Nara, the headquarters of the Shingon Ritsu sect. (Nara City)|Q1203935|In addition to support from Saidaiji Temple}}, it is claimed that they received help from local forces such as Hioka Shrine.{{sfn|Kaneko|2019|pp=13–15}}. It is also speculated that the story of ``Gokai Originki'' is a legendary remnant of the memory that the power of Hioka Shrine and the power of Saidaiji Temple, a Shingon Risshu sect that had a strong faith in Prince Shotoku, jointly carried out construction projects through Bunkan {{sfn|Kaneko|2019|pp=13–15}}.

=== Festival ===
The annual festivals held at Hioka Shrine are as follows <ref>[http://www.hiokajinja.or.jp/event.html Annual Events] (official website). </ref>.
* Monthly
** Monthly Festival (1st of every month)
* January
** Saitan Festival (January 1st)
** Genshi Festival (January 3rd)
** Tondo Festival (January 15th)
*February
** Hatsuuma Festival
** Festival to ward off evil spirits
** '''Imigomori''
**: Special ritual. It is said that this ritual originates from Tenisasahiko-no-Mikoto shutting herself up for seven days as a prayer for the safe delivery of Inahime Tarohime (another theory is that this ritual originates from the enshrining festival of the two pillars of Tamayori-hime and Kusa-Fuga-no-Mikoto{{Sfn|Hioka Zaten Isahiko Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1980}}). It is held from the Pig Day to the Snake Day of the New Year in the lunar calendar. During this period, noise is prohibited at the shrine, and on the Snake Day, which marks the end of the month of mourning, a Shinto ritual is held. </ref>{{Sfn|Hioka Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.
** Prayer Festival (February 17th)
* June
** Natsukoshi Festival (Great Purification Ceremony) (last Saturday and Sunday in June)
* October
** '''Regular Festival''' (2nd Saturday and Sunday in October)
*November
** Shichigosan Shrine
*December
** Great Purification Ceremony (December 31st)
